title: Plausible Analytics
content: Privacy-focused web analytics alternative to Google Analytics. Founded 2019, bootstrapped. Revenue: $100K+/month. Sold for $5M on MicroAcquire. Tech stack: Elixir, Phoenix, ClickDB, PostgreSQL. Pricing: $9/month for 10K pageviews, scaling up. Key insight: positioned as privacy-first (GDPR compliant, no cookies) when Google Analytics was getting complex and privacy-hostile. Target: small to medium websites that care about privacy. Monetization: tiered subscription based on pageviews.

title: Plausible-like Todoist Power-Up
content: A simple Chrome extension that adds time-tracking to Todoist. Built by a solo developer. Revenue: $3K MRR. Sold for $120K. Tech stack: Chrome Extension (Manifest V3), vanilla JS, Firebase. Pricing: $4/month or $36/year. Key insight: Todoist has 35M+ users but no native time tracking. The extension was the #1 rated time-tracking extension on Chrome Web Store. Minimal maintenance - only needed updates when Todoist changed their UI.

title: Transcript.lol
content: AI-powered meeting transcription and summarization tool. Targets remote teams. Revenue: $15K MRR. Tech stack: Next.js, OpenAI Whisper API, Supabase, Stripe. Pricing: $12/month for 10 hours transcription. Key insight: Otter.ai and Fireflies are good but expensive ($16.99+/month). This tool positioned as affordable alternative with better meeting summaries. GTM: Product Hunt launch (500+ upvotes), then SEO targeting 'meeting transcription tool' keywords.
tech_stack: Next.js, OpenAI Whisper API, Supabase, Stripe

title: Resend
content: Email API for developers. Founded 2022, YC W23. Revenue: $1M+ ARR. Pricing: free tier (100 emails/day), $20/month (50K emails). Tech stack: Next.js, Rust (email infrastructure), PostgreSQL, Redis. Key insight: SendGrid and Mailgun have terrible developer experience. Resend focused on beautiful docs, React email components, and modern API. GTM: developer Twitter, Hacker News, open-source React Email library that drove adoption.

title: Cal.com
content: Open-source scheduling tool (Calendly alternative). Founded 2021. Revenue: $2M+ ARR. Pricing: free (self-hosted), $15/user/month (cloud). Tech stack: Next.js, Prisma, PostgreSQL, tRPC. Key insight: Calendly pricing ($10-$46/month) alienated developers and small teams. Cal.com went open-source-first, attracted developers who self-hosted, then upsold cloud hosting. GTM: open-source community, Product Hunt, developer advocacy.

title: Screen Studio
content: Beautiful screen recording tool for Mac. Solo developer (Elias). Revenue: $50K+/month. Pricing: $89 one-time (Pro $139). Tech stack: Swift, macOS native. Key insight: Loom and OBS are functional but produce ugly recordings. Screen Studio auto-zooms, adds smooth cursor animations, and makes recordings look professional. GTM: viral Twitter/X posts of beautiful recordings, Product Hunt #1 of the day. Minimal maintenance - native Mac app with no server costs.

title: Dub.co
content: Open-source link management and shortener. Founded 2022. Revenue: $100K+ ARR. Pricing: free (self-hosted), $24/month (cloud Pro). Tech stack: Next.js, Turso (SQLite edge), Upstash Redis. Key insight: Bitly became enterprise-focused and expensive. Dub.co went open-source, added analytics, custom domains, and API. GTM: open-source GitHub stars, developer Twitter, indie hacker community.
